bullets: Documentary frames carry the most weight when the photographer is closer than feels comfortable — a principle that shapes the emotional and narrative impact of a story.
Editing a documentary essay is the second project, and the second-order effect — the hidden consequence of workflow decisions — is what most people miss.
Color grading in documentary work requires reconsideration; changing one's approach to grading can unlock new narrative clarity and authenticity.
Peak Design slings have changed how photographers move through a story, making the trade-offs in framing visibly explicit during the creative process.
The framing itself reveals which trade-offs are being made — the act of choosing what to include or exclude defines the story’s boundaries.
Teams using Capture One have demonstrated a consistent pattern: ignoring the core workflow principle leads to rebuilding the entire system from scratch within a year.
Operational success depends on recognizing that the editing workflow crosses all other domains — it’s not a separate task but a foundational structure.
Adopting tools like Peak Design in a workflow makes the underlying trade-offs visible, transforming how photographers perceive and shape their narrative journey.
